newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Aleman stays ahead in latest Nicaragua results.
newsitem.headline: Aleman stays ahead in latest Nicaragua results.

text.p: The latest official results on Monday, with more than one third of the votes counted, put right-winger Arnoldo Aleman well ahead of his Sandinista challenger Daniel Ortega in Nicaragua's presidential election.
The Supreme Electoral Council said Aleman had 48.04 percent against Ortega's 39.35 percent with 35.7 percent of the total votes counted by mid-morning.

If borne out by the full count, Aleman's margin of victory will put him well over the 45 percent hurdle needed to secure an outright victory and avoid a second-round runoff against Ortega at the end of November or beginning of December.

Aleman had already claimed victory but Ortega disputed his claim, saying it was too early to say who might have won Sunday's election and claiming that a private Sandinista count of ballots put him slightly ahead.
The electoral council's results bulletin, issued at around 10:45 a.m. local time (1645 GMT), was its third since counting began late on Sunday night.
It was not immediately clear when the count would finish or when it might become possible to discern a definite winner.
